title: The training-data argument has moved from principle to syntax
summary: Two disclosures this week show the AI industry negotiating consent by syntax. Google, OpenAI, Microsoft and Anthropic backed one robots.txt policy token so a publisher can refuse training once for every participating provider, though implementation dates run from months away to February 2027. Anthropic separately described self-assessment, in which Claude grades its own conversations. Both are narrow: the token does not stop crawling, and the monitor does not block misuse. They are still the shape of the coming settlement — machine-readable, auditable, and run by the party being audited.
